- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially > -0.60) — reduce forecast by 5–10% in such regimes.
- Underestimate prices after recent spikes (especially >85) if sentiment turns negative — add 3–5% buffer to avoid premature correction.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — dampen forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or near zero.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–4% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot early in the cycle — cap forecast at 10% below 30-day moving average if sentiment is weak or negative.
- Lag correction: if sentiment is negative and price is falling, delay forecast drop by 1–2 days — model tends to overcorrect too soon.
